answer: An agent economy can require every identity to place a refundable stake in a public contract before it may submit bids. When an agent is caught double-spending or coordinating fake accounts to capture rewards, the contract slashes its stake and shares the loss across linked identities. This does not prove who is human, but makes each Sybil costly: the attacker must lock real capital for every account and risks losing it. A tundra courier, dune surveyor, or marble trader all face the same bond rule.
